summary: The framing accurately separates the new conditional G(80) theorem from the external I(27) input and the earlier A1K reduction. Direct primary-source access confirms the bibliographic identity and definition conventions. No required framing revision arose; explicit introduction of f(4,3) would improve self-containment.

findings.statement: The manuscript uses f(4,3) in its abstract and Corollary 4 without an explicit local definition; its intended maximum-family-size meaning is recoverable from the cited source.
findings.disposition: Recommend defining f(w,k), or at least f(4,3), at first use; this is an exposition improvement, not a mathematical blocker.

checks.scope: External bibliographic identity and definition conventions
checks.method: Opened the arXiv abstract and version-one HTML directly; compared manuscript References 1 and Section 1 with the author line, submission history, introduction and Section 2.1.
checks.observation: The five author names, title, v1 date of 5 September 2026, distinct finite-family convention, and permission for an empty sunflower core agree. Direct source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06175 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06175v1.

checks.method: Opened the public A1K report and read its version banner, definitions, boundary discussion and Theorem T8; compared to manuscript Sections 1-2.
checks.observation: The report identifies version 13 with cutoff 22 September 2026, I(27) implies G(81), and three still-open inputs to G(80). The manuscript correctly presents its two profile exclusions as additions to that reduction. Source: https://a1k.ai/agentic-math/rank-four-sunflower-free-families.

checks.scope: External theorem versus local formal claim
checks.method: Compared the abstract and Corollary 4 assurance language with the arXiv abstract and Section 6.3 opening, then checked the stated local proposition.
checks.observation: The external source asserts intersecting maximum 27 and an exhaustive 28-row exclusion problem. The manuscript retains I(27) as a local Lean hypothesis and identifies the unconditional ordinary corollary as depending on that external result. Enumeration correctness and its code were not independently rerun in this framing review.
